## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
One defect needs fixing before merge: `--wait` is removed outright. The ADR added in this PR says `--wait` stays as a deprecated alias for one release, so existing invocations now fail even though the PR says they keep working. This review read all four changed files in full. It found no other defects in the reviewed scope.

## Critical
- app/cli.py:6 — correctness — Running `parse_args(["--wait", "12"])` now exits with argparse's usage error (`SystemExit` code 2) instead of setting a 12-second timeout, because the `--wait` option was replaced rather than kept as an alias. That contradicts the decision the PR adds in `docs/adr/007-timeout.md:5`: "Accept `--wait` as an alias for one release and emit a deprecation warning when it is used." Fixing this takes two steps: register `--wait` as a second option string for the same `timeout` destination so it still works, and emit a `DeprecationWarning` (or a stderr message) when it is used. Then add a test that `["--wait", "12"]` gives `args.timeout == 12` and triggers the warning. — Any existing script or caller that passes `--wait` breaks immediately with no deprecation period, which is the outcome the ADR says this transition avoids. The `--wait` alias path and its warning also have no regression test.

(none)

## Strengths
- `tests/test_cli.py` still checks the 30-second default, valid values for both `json` and `csv`, and the exit code 2 for a non-integer or missing `--timeout`. So the renamed option keeps the coverage the old one had.
